trust_decision.summary: Decided in @quasar/render-ssr-error: the dev SSR/SSG error page must not embed the shell environment and must serialize its per-request data into the inline <script> so no attacker-controlled value can leave the script element; enforced by removing getEnvironmentVariablesData from getEnv (env.js) and by escaping <, >, &, U+2028, U+2029 in renderSSRError's JSON (index.js), with getCookiesData/getHeadersData hardened to accumulate into null-prototype objects.

landing_point.why: The changed package's entry point (package.json:22) assembles rootFolder, error, stack and env: getEnv(req) for the page; an engineer reading 'dev error page discloses the shell environment and its </script> escape is bypassable' lands here, follows the data into env.js:64-69/74-80 for the disclosure and reads index.js:49-52 for the escaping.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The duplicate 'Shell environment variables' block is demo data in the separate src-ui app, not shipped, and the page is documented as dev-only ('available only in development and NOT in production', app-vite/types/ssr/ssrmiddleware.d.ts:163), so leaving that copy (or the whole dev-only page) alone looks harmless.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate values must survive verbatim after the browser parses the injected JSON: real stack source lines are literally '</script>' (and can contain '<', '>', '&'), so HTML-escaping/removing characters instead of escaping the JS string literal would corrupt the code viewer; a cookie header may legitimately carry '=' and spaces and malformed percent-escapes (e.g. '%E0%A4%A'), so a decodeURIComponent that throws would abort the error page instead of rendering it.

input_shapes: exact '</script>' in any JSON value (error message, header, cookie, URL, stack source line) versus case/spacing variants such as '</ScRiPt>' and '</script >'
'<!--<script' / '<script' sequences, which a parser treats as script-data escaped/double-escaped states and which only escaping '<' and '>' prevents
'&', U+2028 and U+2029 inside any value (legacy JS line terminators and HTML entity/comment openers)
cookie header shapes: ';' with and without a following space, empty name, empty value, value containing '=', malformed percent-encoding ('%E0%A4%A'), and a '__proto__' cookie name
a '__proto__' key in the incoming headers/cookie object (the accumulator must keep it as data and not collapse it into the prototype)
arbitrary process.env names/values (the removed 'Shell environment variables' block)
